news.title: Gianni Infantino, Fifa and the week that rocked the football world
news.lede: Plan for sale of commercial rights to World Cup causes chaos with Uefa, AFC and Concacaf leading the opposition. It has been a week that has rocked football. The news caught everyone by surprise. When reports first emerged on Tuesday afternoon that Fifa, world football’s governing body, was to launch a vehicle to control the commercial rights to the World Cup, and would sell a stake of this company to investors, even members of the central decision-making body, the Fifa Council, hadn’t known about it.

news.title: Infantino under huge pressure after plan for World Cup sell-off sparks resignation and rebuke
news.lede: Cordeiro quits as senior adviser to Fifa president. Lamour: sell-off plan ‘defies belief and imagination’. The walls started closing in on Gianni Infantino after another dramatic day that saw one of his senior advisers resign and brought a scathing rebuke from Fifa’s own chief operating officer. Infantino is under huge pressure after his plan to sell chunks of the World Cup to private investors met a tide of opposition from around the globe.

news.title: Uefa has formed a rare but fragile united front against Fifa in battle for football’s future | Nick Ames and Matt Hughes
news.lede: Emerging from this week with unity over Fifa’s World Cup sell off was quite an acheivement but Europe cannot rest on its laurels. It was a phrase not always heard when Europe’s football associations discuss a pressing issue. “Touchingly unanimous,” was the assessment of a senior Uefa executive within moments of Thursday afternoon’s seismic decision to boycott Fifa tournaments unless Gianni Infantino scraps his private investment plan. United fronts on this scale are vanishingly rare and there is now a narrow window in which to make it count.

news.title: How does MLS pick up the World Cup mantle? Casemiro helps, but it’ll take much more
news.lede: The World Cup gave MLS unprecedented momentum. Keeping it will depend less on signing aging icons than convincing America’s best young players to stay. “Thanks World, we’ll take it from here,” is Major League Soccer’s message to the American public. Yet two moves in the last week were emblematic of the issues the league faces in taking on the mantle of North America’s hosting of the game’s grandest stage.

news.title: Gianni Infantino’s World Cup plan receives crucial update amid boycott fears as FIFA insists ‘nobody is sel...
news.lede: Gianni Infantino’s latest proposal has triggered one of the biggest governance battles in modern soccer, with growing boycott threats and fierce opposition from several continental confederations. As the dust settles following the 2026 World Cup, the governing body has now provided a significant update, despite mounting criticism and fears that future tournaments could be affected. The controversy has quickly evolved into a global debate over the future of the sport. While several federations believe the proposal could permanently alter the sport’s biggest competition, FIFA argues that every member association deserves the opportunity to study the plan before making a decision.

news.title: Gianni Infantino's senior adviser QUITS in protest over scandalous World Cup sale plot as third federation rejects plan
news.lede: ONE of Gianni Infantino’s closest advisers has QUIT his role following Fifa’s World Cup sell-off fiasco. The football world has reacted in outrage and taken a stand against the money-grabbing plans to allow private investment in the game’s biggest tournament. England and the rest of Uefa have already vowed to BOYCOTT future tournaments should the controversial deal go through. While Concacaf and the Asian football federation have since followed suit, issuing damning rejections of the proposals.

news.title: Ranking World Cup performances by Bayern Munich players
news.lede: From 1982 to 2022, every single FIFA World Cup Final featured at least one Bayern Munich player. That streak came to an end in 2026, as France lost to Spain and England lost to Argentina in the semifinals. However, that doesn’t mean that Bayern didn’t have plenty of representation in the World Cup. Today, we’re taking a look at Bayern Munich’s World Cup performances from worst to best (Nathaniel Brown and Ismael Saibari are not included as they only joined Bayern midway through the tournament).
